gone.ask_friend: Have you seen Mabel lately? Could you talk to her for me?
gone.goodbye_note: Chef. I closed my own diner because I couldn't bear to keep it without Walter. I thought yours might be a place like it. I was mistaken. I wish you well, I do. — Mabel

letter.reply: That was an honest letter. I'll come by on Thursday. Have the soup ready.

choices.text: Mabel, I was cruel to you. That was wrong.
Dear Mabel, I'm so, so sorry. I feel terrible!
Mabel! Remember me? Your favorite chef?
There's no excuse for it, and I won't make one.
It's been such a hard few weeks, I haven't been myself.
In my defense, the soup was boiling over.
From now on I'll treat every guest with respect. You first.
I promise I'll be the best chef ever for you!
Next soup's on the house. Forever.

lines.text: Hm. Clean floors. Good start. Don't get excited, dear, I'm only on the floors.
Closed for days without a sign on the door. In my day we'd have put up a sign. Were you ill, or just careless?
I won't pretend last time was good. It wasn't. Let's see what you do with a second chance.
Your last dish was very good. Don't let it go to your head. Heads are heavy enough.
Afternoon, [wrong name].
I'll take the table by the window. I like to watch the door. Old habit.
[name]. You were closed three days. I worried. ...Don't tell anyone I said that.
Afternoon, [name]. Your floors are still clean. I'm keeping score.
Don't fuss, I'll find my own table. I've been finding my own tables for ninety years.
There you are. I came by twice. The second time I just sat on the bench outside. It's a nice bench.
[name]. Sit with me a minute when you're free. I'm in a talking mood.
I brought you something. A pinch of my own seasoning blend. Don't tell anyone where you got it.
You disappeared on me. At my age, dear, you don't do that to people.
There's my favorite cook. Don't tell Walter. ...He'd agree, actually.
I've decided you're one of mine now. That's not up for discussion.
You said "[last_rude_line]" to me. I've been thinking about it. I expected better.
Afternoon.
Good afternoon, chef.
I know your name, dear. I've always known it. It's on your sign. I just wanted to see if you'd tell me the truth when I got it wrong. You did. That's rarer than you'd think. Thank you, [name].
Thank you, [wrong name]. Same time next week. Maybe sooner.
Goodnight, [name]. Taste everything.
Goodnight, [name]. Thank you for listening to an old lady ramble.
Goodnight, dear. Turn the left burner down.
Thank you.
Foam? On a plate? In my day we called that a mistake.
Hm. ...That's very good. Walter would have asked for seconds.
Edible. Solid. Needs a pinch more salt. You'll get there.
It's burnt, dear. I'm going to eat it, because I don't waste food. But it's burnt.
Thank you, [name]. ...You've improved. I won't say it twice.
You burnt it. Good. Even the best of us do. Walter burnt toast every Sunday for fifty years.
[name], this is as good as anything I ever served. I mean that. I don't say things I don't mean.
Thank you.
Your stove runs hot on the left side. Turn it down a notch. Trust me.
I ran a diner for fifty years. Don't look so surprised. I wasn't always this slow. ...I was always this slow.
That bear with the patches. Stitches. He sits alone every time. Someone ought to say hello to him.
That bear with the patches. Stitches. He sits alone every time. Someone ought to say hello to him.
My grandson Cheddar thinks I don't notice his pranks. I notice everything. I let him have it.
You taste everything before it goes out now. I've watched you. That's how I know you'll be fine.
If I had a granddaughter or grandson who cooked like you, I'd be very proud. ...Well. I suppose I do.
Is there something you need, chef? I'm quite comfortable.
Tell me honestly, chef. What's the best thing you make? Not the thing you want to sell me. The best thing.

choices.text: Everything's made with love, so all of it!
choices.reply: Love doesn't season a pot, dear. I'll have the [dish].

choices.text: Honestly? The bread. I bought it.
choices.reply: Well, at least you're honest. The [dish].

choices.text: The [dish]. It's the one I get right every time.
choices.reply: Good. That's the answer I wanted. I'll have it.

choices.text: Just read the menu yourself.
choices.reply: I've survived worse than you, chef. The [dish].

lines.text: Did I ever tell you about the summer of '62? No? Well, there was a storm, and Walter had just— ...well, it'll keep. Soup, please.

choices.text: I'd love to hear it sometime.
choices.reply: Hm. Maybe you will.

choices.text: You can't stop there! That's a cliffhanger!
choices.reply: Patience is a virtue, dear. Soup.

choices.text: I'll get your soup. Tell me the rest when you're ready.
choices.reply: Good answer. Some stories have to be earned.

choices.text: Nobody asked.
choices.reply: No. No one ever does.

lines.text: Thank you, [wrong name]. Now, what's good today?

choices.text: It's [name], but you can call me whatever you like!
choices.reply: I'll call you by your name, dear. I'm not a barbarian.

choices.text: [wrong name] is my evil twin. I'm [name].
choices.reply: Hm. Keep an eye on him, then.

choices.text: It's actually [name].
choices.reply: Is it now. Noted.

choices.text: Can you not even get my name right?
choices.reply: I'm ninety-one, chef. Can you not be kind?

lines.text: Be honest. Are you tired? You look tired. A tired cook burns things.

choices.text: I'm fine, but thank you for caring.
choices.reply: Hm. I'll take your word for it. The [dish].

choices.text: Tired? Me? I'm running on pure soup.
choices.reply: Ha. Well, don't drink the stock.

choices.text: Yeah, honestly. It's been a long week.
choices.reply: Thank you for telling me. Make mine simple today. Soup.

choices.text: Mind your own business.
choices.reply: Hm. I'll have the [dish]. And I'll mind my business.

lines.text: Walter used to say you can tell everything about a cook by their soup. What would yours say about you?

choices.text: That I care about the people I'm feeding.
choices.reply: ...Yes. I think it would. Soup, please.

choices.text: That I need more salt.
choices.reply: Ha! Walter would've liked you.

choices.text: That I'm still learning, but I'm trying.
choices.reply: That's the best thing a cook can be. Soup.

choices.text: That I don't care about your husband's sayings.
choices.reply: ...Soup.

lines.text: I'm going to order the soup, and then you're going to tell me honestly how your week has been. All of it.

choices.text: It's better now that you're here.
choices.reply: Flatterer. ...Thank you, dear.

choices.text: All of it? You might need two bowls.
choices.reply: Then bring two.

choices.text: (Tell her honestly that it was hard.)
choices.reply: Thank you for telling me. Hard weeks end. Good soup helps.

choices.text: You're not my grandma.
choices.reply: ...No. I suppose I'm not.

lines.text: The [dish], please. Thank you.
The [dish].
Have you seen my glasses? I had them when I came in.

choices.text: They're on your head, Mabel.
Have you tried looking up?
(Say nothing.)

lines.text: Can I give you some advice? You don't have to take it.

choices.text: I'd love that, Mabel.
choices.reply: Taste everything before it leaves your kitchen. Everything. That's it. That's the advice.

choices.text: Is it 'more salt'? It's always more salt.
choices.reply: It's sometimes more salt. Today it's not.

choices.text: Yes. Tell me what I'm doing wrong.
choices.reply: You rush the plating. Food deserves a second look before it goes out.

choices.text: I don't need advice from you.
choices.reply: No. You don't need anything from me.

lines.text: I haven't cooked for anyone since Walter. Not even myself. That's why I come here, I suppose.

choices.text: I'm glad you come here.
choices.reply: So am I, dear.

choices.text: Maybe you could cook something with me sometime.
choices.reply: ...Maybe. Don't push your luck.

choices.text: That's kind of sad.
choices.reply: Yes. It is.

lines.text: Recommend me something. And tell me why. A recommendation without a reason is just a guess.

favorite.text: Soup. Of course you'd pick soup. You've been paying attention.

disliked.text: Hm. You're brave. Wrong, but brave.

lines.text: I know your name, dear. I've always known it. It's on your sign. I just wanted to see if you'd tell me the truth when I got it wrong. You did. That's rarer than you'd think. Thank you, [name].
[restaurant]. Hm. Good name. Easy to say, easy to remember. Walter would have approved.
In my day the diner was just called 'Diner.' [restaurant] is better. Don't let it go to your head.
Afternoon. [restaurant] smells right today. That's a compliment, dear.
This is Mabel. I would like to place an order for delivery.
Good evening. Mabel speaking. Delivery, please.
Received. Thank you for not making excuses. ...[dish], please.
Soup. No bread. Thank you.
[dish]. The left burner still runs hot.
That will be all.

choices.text: (Tuck a note in her bag: "I was wrong, and I'm sorry.")
(Tuck a note in her bag: "I'm so sorry, Mabel! We miss you here!")
(Just send the food.)
(Tuck a note in the bag: "Find another diner.")

lines.text: It's Mabel, dear. Nothing to order. I only wanted to hear how my kitchen's doing. ...Your kitchen. Turn the left burner down. Goodnight.
Well. I'm here. Say what you came to say, and say it plainly.

choices.text: I was cruel to you. I'm sorry. No excuses.
choices.reply: ...Thank you. That's how it's done.

choices.text: I've missed you, Mabel. This place isn't the same.
choices.reply: Hm. It isn't. I could tell from the floors.

choices.text: Can I make you some soup?
choices.reply: ...Yes. You can.

lines.text: We'll start again. Afternoon, Gerald.
